unavailable: Can’t read scheduled tasks right now (the database isn’t responding). Try again in a bit.
save_failed: Couldn’t save scheduled tasks. Your change wasn’t applied. Please try again.
daily_title: A daily task needs a title
interval_range: The interval must be between {min} minutes and 7 days
time_passed: That time has passed. Pick a later one.
until_passed: That end time has passed. Pick a later one, or clear it.
missed: Persona was down and missed the time
busy_skipped: The last run is still going, so this one was skipped
busy_wait: The last run is still going. Try again when it’s done.
gone: This scheduled task no longer exists
not_ready_skipped: Your computer or model isn’t set up yet, so this one was skipped
ready_again: Your computer and model are set up, so scheduled tasks run again, starting with “{name}”
ready_again_unnamed: Your computer and model are set up, so scheduled tasks run again
streak: “{name}” hasn’t gone through {count} runs in a row
streak_body: Last one: {reason}. I won’t bring this up again until it goes through once.
deleted_not_again: {id}「{name}」 was deleted by the user while this run was going, so nothing was scheduled. Don't schedule it again; just finish this run.
waiting_skipped: {name} didn't run this time: its last run is waiting for you
waiting_skipped_body: Its last run is waiting for your approval or answer. Once you handle it, the next run goes as usual. Open it to see what it needs.
cron_empty: Write a cron expression, like 0 9 * * 1-5 (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week)
cron_zone: {cron} sets its own time zone. Leave out TZ= / CRON_TZ=: cron tasks run in your time zone.
cron_every: @every isn’t a cron schedule. To repeat every N minutes (at least {min}), use an interval instead.
cron_alias: {cron} isn’t a cron alias. Use @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly or @yearly, or 5 fields like 0 9 * * 1-5.
cron_fields: {cron} has {n} fields. A cron expression has 5: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week (like 0 9 * * 1-5; seconds aren’t supported).
cron_field: In {cron}, the {field} can’t be {value}. Use a number in its range, *, a list (1,15), a range (9-18) or a step (*/30).
cron_day_of_week: day of week (0–7 or SUN–SAT, 0 and 7 are Sunday)
cron_often: {cron} runs {gap} minutes apart. A scheduled task runs at most every {min} minutes.
cron_never: {cron} never runs: no date in the next 5 years matches it.
